clue.text: Fearful type that rings the alarm

explanation.surface: A nervous person is the sort to raise the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A trembler is a timid, quaking person, and also the vibrating hammer of an electric bell that makes it ring.

clue.text: Something brewing in the witches' cauldron ?

definitions.text: Something brewing in the witches' cauldron ?

parts.words: Something brewing in the witches' cauldron ?
parts.note: recalls the witches' chant in Macbeth, 'Double, double toil and ...', and brewing also means mischief building up

explanation.surface: A question about the contents of the witches' pot in Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is brewing when difficulty is building, and the word ends the Macbeth witches' refrain.

clue.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

definitions.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

parts.words: Return to the country, the scene of the crime
parts.note: sending a suspect back to the nation where the offence took place, for trial there

explanation.surface: A criminal drawn back to where the deed was done.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over a fugitive to the state where they are accused is the legal process of surrender abroad.

clue.text: Blasted din es guns try to, get the range

definitions.text: es guns try to, get the range

parts.note: blasted is a mild oath, the kind printed as b—, so it gives B
a racket is a din or loud noise

explanation.surface: The deafening noise of guns finding their target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'es' is the OCR's misreading of 'as'. Bracketing is firing shots over and short of a target to find the range.
explanation.definitionFit: In gunnery a bracket is a pair of shots either side of the target used to fix the range.

clue.text: Confer peerage at levée?

indicators.note: the question mark tells the solver the words before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ennobling someone at a royal morning reception.
explanation.walkthrough: A levée is a formal reception held by a monarch; AT LEVEE rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage is to lift them in rank.

clue.text: Many introduce world shortage

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many
the world is the earth, our planet

explanation.surface: Overpopulation brings global scarcity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduce' joins the pieces: D comes first, then EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: Rent collection, said in France to be without strain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the French word sits round the other piece

parts.note: dit is French for said

explanation.surface: Gathering rents is stress-free, according to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: DIT goes round STRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraint is seizing goods to recover unpaid rent or debt.

clue.text: Rustic paradise in kind of light opera turn'

parts.note: an arc light is a bright electric lamp

indicators.note: to turn the opera's name is to read it backwards

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: An idyllic pastoral world inside some operetta number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses AIDA to ADIA, after ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised rural region of Greek pastoral poetry.

clue.text: Rows. upon rows upon rows of rowers in this

definitions.text: Rows. upon rows upon rows of rowers in this

parts.words: Rows. upon rows upon rows of rowers in this
parts.note: three banks of oarsmen stacked one above another, the rows counted three times

explanation.surface: A vessel crowded with tier upon tier of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: On strike, a rogue's in trouble. Monstrous!

parts.note: workers who have walked out are out

indicators.note: being in trouble means the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A villain who downs tools and gets into hot water is a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reworks A ROGUES into RAGEOUS, after OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monstrous is shocking beyond all bounds, a synonym.

clue.text: High-speed pen-holder

explanation.surface: A fast fountain pen holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at a fair clip means moving fast; a clip is also the metal grip that holds a pen in a pocket.

clue.text: Unmarked type of paper for a harmless report

parts.note: a blank sheet has no marks on it
cartridge paper is a thick drawing paper

explanation.surface: Plain stationery suited to an inoffensive written account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is the bang of a gun, not a document, which is what makes the paper surface mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank cartridge has powder but no bullet, so its firing makes only a noise.

clue.text: The Pauline line

parts.note: a line is a short letter ('drop me a line'), and the Pauline ones are the apostle Paul's letters in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A phrase about the doctrine of St Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's New Testament letters are known by this formal word for a letter.

clue.text: Rule is changed, see, without haste

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of these words are altered into a new order

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A regulation is amended, look, so nobody needs to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' reworks RULE IS into LEISUR; a see is a bishop's diocese, here Ely.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried, relaxed in pace.

clue.text: Not one of our rising: young men

definitions.text: Not one of our rising: young men

parts.words: Not one of our rising: young men
parts.note: rising is read as getting out of bed, not advancing in a career: this person stays under the covers

explanation.surface: A lament that someone is no promising young high-flier.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is a person who stays in bed late, the opposite of an early riser.

clue.text: Banger eat-in perhaps? Buzz, buzz

parts.note: a banger is an explosive firework, a kind of bomb

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A sausage restaurant, maybe, alive with chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' looks like the British sausage; it is an explosive, BOMB. 'perhaps' reworks EATIN into INATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombinate is to hum or drone, as bees do.

clue.text: Cash in advance for assistance with homework

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective: what was cashed in advance is prepaid

parts.note: prep, short for preparation, is homework in British schools
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Paying up front for help with school assignments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins AID to PREP; PREP is the British boarding-school word for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepaid means settled before the goods or service arrive.

clue.text: Get, back or better

explanation.surface: Retrieve something or get well.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain something lost, or to get well after illness.

clue.text: Small portion of hen ?

explanation.surface: A little helping of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A partlet is a small part, and Dame Partlet is a hen in old fable, so the name means a hen.

clue.text: Here's a go

parts.note: having a go means trying, so this is an announcement that someone is trying their hand

explanation.surface: Someone offering a turn at something.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try or a go at something.

clue.text: Cut a tea arrangement and get working

indicators.note: an arrangement of these letters puts them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Slicing up a tea party and getting started.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate a machine is to set it in motion.

clue.text: A bit of a climber? Net return, endless square-bashing

indicators.note: return means the word before it is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written before turning

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: square-bashing is British slang for military drill on the parade ground

explanation.surface: A mountaineer brings back a net after endless parade drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NET to TEN; 'endless' cuts DRILL to DRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the coiling shoot a climbing plant uses to cling.

clue.text: Everyone in the river — most improbable

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout
everyone is all

explanation.surface: The whole crowd in the water would be hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: A tall story is an unlikely one, so tallest is most improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale is hard to believe, so the superlative means the least credible.

clue.text: What evidence' of. Touchstone's lie ?

explanation.surface: A question about proving that a jester told a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's As You Like It, the clown Touchstone lists degrees of lie, among them the Lie Circumstantial.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumstantial evidence points to a fact indirectly, and the Lie Circumstantial is one of Touchstone's named grades of lie.

clue.text: Ineradicable in a money economy? That's bad!

explanation.surface: Grumbling that greed can never be rooted out of a cash society.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on the saying 'money is the root of all evil': what money roots cannot be eradicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked or bad, and in the proverb it is what the love of money is the root of.

clue.text: Discourse at length about might of an exile

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the long-winded word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Holding forth on the power of someone banished.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'right', which the OCR read as 'might'; R goes inside EXPATIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate lives away from their native land, as an exile does.

clue.text: Fairly attractive

explanation.surface: Reasonably good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means fairly, as in 'pretty good', and also good-looking.

clue.text: Tom takes wine here, with sundry guys in support

definitions.text: here, with sundry guys in support

parts.note: Great Tom is a famous bell at Christ Church, Oxford, so Tom stands for a bell
tent is an old name for a deep-red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A man drinks in a place propped up by a gang of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the two pieces. The guys are guy ropes, not men, holding up a round tent on a central pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tent is a conical tent held upright by a pole and many guy ropes.
